Flows with a manual trigger are intended to be executable only by an authenticated user. The authentication check in the
manual trigger handler only verified that an accountability object was present on the request. Unauthenticated API
requests are assigned a default public accountability object, which satisfied that check, so anonymous callers were not
rejected. Authorization then fell through to the permission check, which resolves an accountability object without a
user or role to the Public role.

As a result, an unauthenticated request to the public trigger endpoint (`POST /flows/trigger/:id`) could execute an
active manual Flow whenever the Flow is enabled for a collection that the Public role can read.

This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-53889 (GHSA-7cvf-pxgp-42fc). The guard introduced in 11.9.0 added a permission
check on the target collection and items, but did not distinguish public accountability from an authenticated identity.

Flows using the Webhook trigger are publicly triggerable by design and are not affected.

## Impact

An unauthenticated attacker can execute automation that was intended to be available only to logged in users, and can
repeat that execution at will.

The consequences depend on how the Flow is configured. Operations in a Flow can be set to run with full permissions, in
which case they execute regardless of the caller's access rights. A manual Flow built for staff use can therefore give
an anonymous caller read, create, update or delete access to data that the Public role cannot reach directly. Flows can
also perform other side effecting actions, such as outbound HTTP requests, notifications and mail, which become
anonymously reachable.

Exploitation requires all of the following:

- An active Flow with a manual trigger exists.
- The Flow is enabled for a collection that the Public role has read access to.
- The attacker knows the Flow's ID.
- If the Flow requires item selection, the attacker also needs the ID of an item in that collection that the Public role
  can read.

Projects that expose public content collections while using manual Flows for privileged editorial, moderation, approval,
notification or integration actions are the most exposed.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, any of the following reduce or remove exposure:

- Remove Public role read access from collections that are selected on manual Flows.
- Disable manual Flows that are attached to publicly readable collections, or convert them to a trigger type that is not
  publicly reachable.
- Review manual Flows for operations that run with full permissions and scope them down.

## References

- https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/27997
- https://github.com/directus/directus/security/advisories/GHSA-7cvf-pxgp-42fc (CVE-2025-53889)

## Credit
